newsitem.title: NORWAY: Nycomed says three largest shareholders informed.
newsitem.headline: Nycomed says three largest shareholders informed.

text.p: Norwegian drugs company Nycomed ASA said on Tuesday it had informed over the last few days its three largest shareholders of a proposed merger with Britain's Amersham International Plc.
Nycomed's three largest shareholders are the Norwegian state pension fund, Folketrygdfondet, insurer Storebrand and food and beverage-based conglomerate Orkla ASA,
"The companies understand the industrial arguements," Nycomed CEO Svein Aaser told a news conference.

In 1995 the then energy-drugs company Hafslund Nycomed and Ivax Corp of the United States proposed a merger of their healthcare businesses. The companies subsequently called off the deal due to a lack of sharecholder support.
Hafslund Nycomed later demerged to form power generator Hafslund ASA and drugs company Nycomed.
Aaser said the shareholders had been informed of the proposal but had not yeat seen the final merger document.
